svg.title: Pellier hybrid retrieval flow
svg.desc: A shopper request provides query terms and hard constraints. Bedrock Cohere Embed produces the query vector. Aurora applies catalog eligibility predicates to PostgreSQL full-text and pgvector retrieval, then merges ranks using RRF. Bedrock Cohere Rerank reorders the bounded candidate pool. A Strands specialist grounds the response in the returned products and exposes exact evidence. Participants inspect candidate IDs, query plans, and ranking tradeoffs.
svg.text: Pellier: how a hybrid search result is produced
Anna’s retrieval path | The same ranking stages are implemented in the backend and the managed Lambda tools
Apply catalog, price, stock, and archive constraints in both branches
Merge ranks into a bounded candidate pool
Ground the answer in returned products.
Keep product IDs and source evidence.
Expose the matching turn in Observatory.
Compare lexical, vector, and fused IDs.
Find where an eligible item disappeared.
Inspect filtering, index use, and buffers.
Hold the request and constraints fixed.
Compare relevance, pool size, and latency.
A reranker cannot recover a product that never entered the candidate pool.
Record the request, returned IDs, constraints, and query plan. Use supplied checks; participants do not build an evaluation framework.
Design decision: enforce eligibility before ranking, then inspect each stage independently.
